items.s: The statue was so ____ that it would not fit through the door of an ordinary house.
Old coins can be very ____ to a museum, even when they are small.
Guards were sent to ____ the site so that nobody could steal anything.
The guide was asked to ____ why the statue was so big.
Only the ____ of the old wall were left, and most of it had fallen down.

match.d: remove something from under the ground
gone permanently and impossible to recover
unusual enough to be worth noticing

items.s: He could have ____ the stone away or kept it.
His decision ____ archaeologists to something remarkable.
Ramesses II ____ more than 3,000 years ago.
He ____ for building impressive temples and monuments.
Archaeologists still have plenty of work ____.

tfn.s: One of the statue heads was more than one and a half metres tall.
tfn.why: The text says: "One statue head was about 1.6 metres tall."

tfn.s: The complete statue may once have been taller than a two-storey house.
tfn.why: The text says it may have stood around 8.5 metres high, "which is taller than a two-storey house".

tfn.s: Archaeologists found the statues close to a temple linked to a goddess.
tfn.why: The text says: "The objects were found near the remains of a temple linked to Isis, an important goddess in ancient Egyptian religion."

tfn.s: The statues will be moved to a museum in Cairo.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say where the statues will be kept after the excavation.

tfn.s: The resident kept the stone and sold it privately.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "Instead, he reported it to the experts, and his decision led archaeologists to something remarkable."

pre.d: a person who lives in a place
people who study the past by looking at old things in the ground
a very hard grey or pink stone
a female god
big buildings or statues made to remember a person or event

focus.note: A phrasal verb is a verb plus a small word, like out or away. The small word changes the meaning, so learn them together.

items.s: The experts will ____ out how old the statue is.
Please do not carry the stones ____; leave them where you found them.
It looked like an ordinary stone, but it turned ____ to be a piece of history.
The team will carry ____ with the dig next week.
The guide asked us to ____ after the stone, because it is very old.
The vase was broken into dozens of small ____, which the museum staff carefully glued together.
The roof was leaking badly, so the repair was ____ and could not wait until spring.
The police found no ____ that anyone had broken into the house.
Doctors were not worried because it was a single, ____ incident and not part of a pattern.
Engineers ____ that the repairs will cost around two million pounds.
He was ____ the best candidate, since he had the most experience, but the interviews were not finished.

match.d: help explain something that was unclear
be found or appear, often when nobody expected it
arrange or plan how parts are placed in an area
made to look attractive rather than to be used

items.s: By the time the experts arrived, the resident ____ the authorities.
The ruins ____ by law since they were declared a national monument.
If the man had sold the stone, researchers ____ the statues.
When the rain began, the specialists still ____ the layers of earth.
Last year, an old coin ____ in a garden in our town.

tfn.s: Experts think the whole statue may have been over eight metres high.
tfn.why: The text says: "Archaeologists estimate that the complete figure may originally have been approximately 8.5 metres tall."

tfn.s: The resident received a payment from the antiquities authority.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say whether the resident was paid.

tfn.s: Specialists inspected the stone before they started a rescue excavation.
tfn.why: The text says: "Specialists from Egypt's Supreme Council of Antiquities inspected the original stone and then carried out a rescue excavation."

tfn.s: Researchers already know exactly where the statues stood.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "There is still work to do before researchers can explain precisely where the statues stood and what purpose they served."

tfn.s: The writer thinks an object found by chance is likely to teach researchers less than one found during a proper excavation.
tfn.why: The text says such an object "may still be beautiful, but it is likely to tell researchers very little".

pre.d: with words or marks cut into the surface
the work of digging carefully to find things from the past
the pictures and symbols used in ancient Egyptian writing
an old object made by people
very important in a religion
the time when a king or queen rules
in a careful, organised way, step by step

focus.note: Many phrasal verbs have a meaning you cannot guess from the parts. Learn the whole verb, for example look into means to investigate.

items.s: The team will ____ out a rescue excavation before the builders arrive.
Experts will ____ into the history of the statue before they publish anything.
Without a record, a find can ____ up in a private collection.
The authorities asked the public to come ____ if they had information.
The archaeologist pointed ____ that the statue was once much taller.
The festival is closely ____ with the harvest, though its exact origins remain unclear.
An internal audit ____ a pattern of irregular payments that nobody had noticed.
It took the inquiry months to ____ who had authorised the transfer.
Only ____ of the original manuscript survive, so scholars must reconstruct much of the argument.
Careful ____ between the two sets of figures revealed a small but consistent gap.
On that ____, even a minor error would have serious consequences.

match.d: order and pay for something to be made specially
a sacred place such as a temple or shrine

items.s: Scholars have questioned the ____ of the traditional dating of the monument.
The ____ of the fragments in the soil suggests they were moved long ago.

tfn.s: The writer implies that a head displayed in a museum may have lost part of its historical value.
tfn.why: The text says a head in a museum may be impressive, but its original position "could answer questions the carving alone cannot".

tfn.s: The complete figure was more than five times taller than the head that was found.
tfn.why: The head was about 1.6 metres tall and the figure about 8.5 metres, and 8.5 divided by 1.6 is just over five.

tfn.s: The original arrangement of the statues is already well understood.
tfn.why: The text says the fragments "do not yet give a complete picture of the statues or their original arrangement".

tfn.s: The resident was paid a reward by the Supreme Council of Antiquities.
tfn.why: The text does not say whether the resident received any payment.

tfn.s: Experts have ruled out changing their explanation of the site.
tfn.why: The text says further excavation and comparisons "may change the explanation".

focus.note: At this level, many phrasal verbs are fairly formal. Check whether the meaning is literal or figurative: brush aside means to dismiss something.

items.s: Investigators refused to ____ aside the possibility that the damage was deliberate.
Many of the site's problems ____ from decades of neglect.
Officials were accused of trying to ____ down the seriousness of the damage.
The findings should not ____ out further excavation at the site.
Careful recording can ____ about a far better understanding of the site.

speak.title: Role-play: what should we do with the stone?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your neighbour has found a strange stone with writing on it. You think it could be worth a lot of money. Try to persuade your neighbour to keep it or sell it. Ask at least two questions.

b.text: You found a strange stone with writing on it near your home. You want to report it to the experts. Explain why, and answer your neighbour's ideas politely.

phrases: I think it could be worth a lot of money.
I'd rather call the experts first.
That's not a good idea, because we don't know what it is.
Let's find out what it is before we decide.
We could both agree to ask for advice.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: what did you decide to do with the stone, and why?
